rules.title: Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for landlords to use or for anyone to sell, license, or provide coordinated pricing algorithms that set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Tenants may sue for damages or penalties if a landlord uses such an algorithm.
rules.key_value: Total ban on use or sale of coordinated pricing algorithms for rent/occupancy setting
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to software that only publishes aggregated/anonymous data, sets affordable housing limits, or is used for market research, appraisal, or software development (if not used for recommendations to landlords).
rules.interaction: This ordinance does not regulate the amount of rent that a landlord may charge, only the use and sale of coordinated pricing algorithms.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about, use, or require disclosure of criminal history in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties limited exemptions; owner-occupied properties (between 1-3 units) in which an owner of record resides in one of the units as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: 2026 Adjustments of Relocation Assistance Payments
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay a standard relocation assistance payment of $19,413 to tenants displaced by owner move-in or Ellis Act evictions starting January 1, 2026. Qualifying households are entitled to an additional $6,471.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants displaced by owner move-in or Ellis Act evictions.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction. The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market. Both ordinances index the relocation payments to inflation, and provide that the Rent Board shall publish the yearly inflationary increases. At its October 16, 2025 Special Meeting, the Rent Board approved relocation assistance payment increases that will go into effect on January 1, 2026. The standard relocation assistance payment will increase to $19,413. The additional relocation assistance payment for qualifying households will increase to $6,471.

rules.title: Maximum tenant screening fee for 2026
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge more than $68.96 as a tenant screening fee in 2026. If a tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it and cannot charge a new fee.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley.
rules.interaction: This rule supplements California Civil Code Section 1950.6.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenants
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for renewing a tenancy, including fees for roommate changes.
rules.key_value: No non-refundable renewal or roommate fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Cap at 5%
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for fully covered units are capped at 5%, even if the formula would otherwise allow more. Landlords may still use 'banked' increases from prior years to reach the rent ceiling.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully covered rental units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to partially covered or exempt units. Banked AGAs from prior years may allow increases above 5%.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76 (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

rules.title: Eviction for Nonpayment of Rent Threshold
rules.requirement: A landlord may only evict for nonpayment of rent if the tenant owes at least one month of Fair Market Rent for a comparable unit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully or partially covered units under the Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to exempt units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76 (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

rules.title: No Eviction for Failure to Sign Substantially Similar Lease
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot evict tenants for failing to sign a substantially similar lease at the end of a fixed-term lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully or partially covered units under the Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to exempt units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76 (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

rules.title: Material Lease Breach Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: Eviction for breach of lease is allowed only if the breach is of a mutually agreed term, causes substantial actual damage, and the landlord shows the tenant's behavior was unreasonable.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully or partially covered units under the Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to exempt units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76 (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: Material lease terms only include mutually agreed upon lease terms. The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable.

rules.title: Eviction Notice Content and Filing Requirements
rules.requirement: Eviction notices must include Rent Board contact information and be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service to the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully or partially covered units under the Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to exempt units.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76 (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: Any notice terminating a tenancy must contain a statement that advice about the notice is available from the Rent Board, the current phone number for the Rent Board’s Housing counseling services, and the current address of the Rent Board’s website. The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.

rules.title: Notice of Tenant Rights Requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies starting on or after December 20, 2024, landlords must provide a written Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days of tenancy start and post it in any interior common area.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all new tenancies in fully or partially covered units starting on or after December 20, 2024.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to exempt units or tenancies started before December 20, 2024.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.76 (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies started on or after December 20, 2024, landlords must, within fifteen days of the start of the tenancy, give the tenant written notice containing the following information: The existence of and scope of the Rent Ordinance; the tenant’s right to petition against certain rent increases, if applicable; whether the unit is exempt from rent control; and any other partial exemptions which may exist. If the property has an interior common area that all tenants have access to, the landlord must post the notice in the common area.

rules.title: Security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: Landlord requirement to photograph unit before or at the start of a new tenancy
rules.requirement: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.
rules.coverage_conditions: All new tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

rules.title: Landlord requirement to photograph unit after regaining possession before repairs/cleaning for deposit deductions
rules.requirement: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit. These photos and a written explanation of the cost of the repairs/cleaning must be given to the tenant along with the itemized statement.
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenancies where deductions from the security deposit are made after April 1, 2025.
rules.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit. These photos and a written explanation of the cost of the repairs/cleaning must be given to the tenant along with the itemized statement.

rules.title: 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: For eligible rental units, the maximum allowable rent increase for 2026 is 1.0%, effective no earlier than January 1, 2026. Landlords may not apply this increase to tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025, if their rent was set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to eligible rental units subject to Berkeley rent stabilization.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025, where rent was set under Costa-Hawkins.
rules.interaction: The 1.0% limit is based on 65% of the Bay Area CPI increase from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code section 13.76.110A; Rent Board Regulation 1148
rules.quoted_span: the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026. The 2026 AGA of 1.0% represents 65% of the increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers in the Bay Area during the period from July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025, which was 1.5% as posted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Exemption applies if rent was set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.

rules.title: Rent Control for Multifamily Properties Built Before 1980
rules.requirement: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 are subject to rent control under Berkeley's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 are covered.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplexes, owner-occupied shared kitchen/bath, certain ADUs, university units, nonprofit cooperatives, and some subsidized units with HUD-insured or held mortgages are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes
rules.unstructured_conditions: Some government-subsidized units are exempt if the project has a mortgage insured or held by HUD.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Protections for Multifamily Properties Built Before 1980
rules.requirement: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 are protected by just cause eviction rules under Berkeley's ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 are covered.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplexes, owner-occupied shared kitchen/bath, certain ADUs, university units, nonprofit cooperatives, and some subsidized units with HUD-insured or held mortgages are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes
rules.unstructured_conditions: Some government-subsidized units are exempt if the project has a mortgage insured or held by HUD.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy units may not deny housing based on arrests not resulting in conviction, expunged/sealed convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old, unless there is a direct relationship to safety or the housing sought.
rules.key_value: No blanket denial for arrests, expunged/sealed, juvenile, or >5-year-old convictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to current criminal behavior; preempted by conflicting federal or state law.
rules.interaction: Federal or state law preempts this policy where there is a conflict.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Coverage depends on whether the building receives DND funding or has BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units; this cannot be determined from year_built, units, or use_code.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy – Credit Screening
rules.requirement: Agents may not use applicant credit score to approve or deny housing applications. Credit history may only be used in lieu of rental history to determine ability to pay rent when rental history is not available.
rules.key_value: Credit score may not be used; credit history only if no rental history
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Preempted by conflicting federal or state law.
rules.interaction: Federal or state law preempts this policy where there is a conflict.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span: The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing applications. Property Managers may consider an applicant’s credit history, but such information may ONLY be used in lieu of rental history to determine an applicant’s ability to pay rent when rental history is not available.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Coverage depends on whether the building receives DND funding or has BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units; this cannot be determined from year_built, units, or use_code.

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement: A bill that would have authorized Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections did not become law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to rental housing in Boston if enacted.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

rules.title: Boston Fair Housing Regulations – Source of Income Discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston may not refuse to rent to tenants because they use rental assistance such as Section 8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, or veterans vouchers.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing in Boston.
rules.exemptions: No exemptions for multifamily apartment buildings are stated. Exemptions for non-housing or out-of-Boston discrimination are mentioned but not relevant here.
rules.interaction: This rule enforces local, state, and federal fair housing laws in Boston.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance. This includes Section 8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act tenant notice requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or Notice of non-renewal of lease.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords ending a tenancy agreement must comply.
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires ALL LANDLORDS planning to end a tenancy agreement to provide the tenant with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act city notification requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords and foreclosing owners must submit tenant contact information and a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of non-renewal of lease to the City using the online portal.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy agreement must comply.
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act also requires landlords and foreclosing owners to complete the Notice to Quit / Non-renewal of Lease Submission Verification Form. Landlords must use this online form to provide tenant contact information and upload a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act – Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as serving a Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease. Landlords must also send a copy of the notice and a Certificate of Compliance/Service to the City of Boston’s Office of Housing Stability.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords or foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.quoted_span: The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination based on protected characteristics in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Landlords and tenant screening companies may not screen prospective tenants in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic, including race, national origin, disability, source of income, and others.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most providers of housing and services related to housing, including landlords and tenant screening companies, for the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied single-family homes renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics. Senior housing and housing for homeless youth may have age-based restrictions. Shared living area in a single dwelling may allow sex-based preference.
rules.quoted_span: Screening prospective tenants – including when done by a third-party such as a tenant screening company – in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic

rules.title: Prohibition on source of income discrimination in rental housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent to a tenant or apply different terms based on the tenant's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most housing accommodations in California, including multifamily apartments.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied single-family homes renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics. Senior housing and housing for homeless youth may have age-based restrictions. Shared living area in a single dwelling may allow sex-based preference.
rules.quoted_span: Can a housing provider refuse to rent to someone because of their source of income? No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.

rules.title: Limitations on use of criminal history in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Landlords may not have blanket bans on renting to people with a criminal history and may not consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records. Denials based on criminal convictions must be directly related to tenancy and safety.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most housing accommodations in California, including multifamily apartments.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied single-family homes renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics. Senior housing and housing for homeless youth may have age-based restrictions. Shared living area in a single dwelling may allow sex-based preference.
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history. If a housing provider intends to deny someone’s application based on a criminal conviction, it must be directly-related to someone’s ability to be a good tenant and to not be a threat to the health and safety of others and the property.

rules.title: Cartwright Act: violations – prohibition on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of the Cartwright Act. It is also unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if coercing another to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm for products or services in California.
rules.exemptions: Does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.interaction: This rule expands the scope of activities prohibited by the Cartwright Act and does not limit the applicability of other antitrust laws.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter. (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

rules.title: Statewide Just Cause for Eviction (2026 amendment)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written notice. Just cause includes both at-fault and no-fault grounds, and relocation assistance or rent waiver is required for no-fault terminations.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months; relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most multifamily residential rental properties statewide after 12 months of occupancy.
rules.exemptions: Exempts new construction (15 years), certain owner-occupied, single-family, and deed-restricted affordable housing, and properties with qualifying local just cause ordinances.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a more protective ordinance adopted after that date, is in effect.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Exemption for single-family homes requires written notice to tenants as specified in the statute.

rules.title: Statewide rent cap (2024-2030): CPI+5% or 10%, whichever is lower
rules.requirement: For most apartments built more than 15 years ago, the landlord may not increase rent by more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living (CPI), or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period. No more than two rent increases are allowed in a 12-month period for the same tenant.
rules.key_value: lesser of 5% + CPI or 10% per year
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most multifamily rental housing statewide, except as listed in exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Exempts deed-restricted affordable housing, dormitories, housing under stricter local rent control, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain single-family homes, and owner-occupied duplexes.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local rent control ordinance restricts increases to a lower amount.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Security deposit cap for residential rentals
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to security collected or demanded by the landlord before July 1, 2024. Exception for certain small landlords (see below).
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Exception to security deposit cap for small landlords
rules.requirement: If the landlord is a natural person or a limited liability company in which all members are natural persons, and owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent, the landlord may demand or receive security in an amount up to two months’ rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member. Does not apply to security collected or demanded by the landlord before July 1, 2024.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to two months’ rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy if the landlord meets both of the following requirements: (i) The landlord is a natural person or a limited liability company in which all members are natural persons. (ii) The landlord owns no more than two residential rental properties that collectively include no more than four dwelling units offered for rent.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Only applies if the landlord is a natural person or LLC of natural persons and owns no more than two properties with a total of four or fewer units.

rules.title: Security deposit return deadline and itemization
rules.requirement: The landlord must return any remaining portion of the security deposit and provide an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, no later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to the expiration of a fixed-term lease, the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant as follows:

rules.title: Prohibition on nonrefundable security deposits
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as 'nonrefundable.'
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
rules.quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Limits on application screening fees for residential rental applicants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge an application screening fee greater than $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI, and may only charge actual out-of-pocket costs. The landlord must provide a receipt itemizing expenses and return any unused portion if no reference check or credit report is performed. No fee may be charged if no unit is available, and fees must be refunded or credited if the application is not considered, with specific timelines for refunds.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental applicants statewide.
rules.exemptions: This section is not intended to preempt any provisions or regulations that govern the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination based on source of income and requirements for screening applicants with government rent subsidies
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a financial or income standard that is not based on the tenant's portion of rent when there is a government rent subsidy, and must allow applicants to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay if credit history is used.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: The law does not limit the ability to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify identity. It is not discrimination to inquire about the level or source of income.
rules.quoted_span: (o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant. (B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination based on source of income in rental housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on lawful, verifiable sources of income, including housing subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: It is not discrimination to make a written or oral inquiry concerning the level or source of income.
rules.quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the ... source of income ... of that person. ... (c) For any person to make, print, or publish, or cause to be made, printed, or published any notice, statement, or advertisement, with respect to the sale or rental of a housing accommodation that indicates any preference, limitation, or discrimination based on ... source of income ...

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance – Source of Income Discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental agents may not discriminate against applicants based on source of income, including Section 8 and public benefits, when renting housing in Cambridge.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing transactions in Cambridge, including viewing or renting an apartment and terms and conditions of tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there. Other exemptions for hotels, hospitals, dormitories, etc. may apply but are not relevant to multifamily apartments.
rules.quoted_span: The protected categories under the Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance and the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance are the following: ... Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits

rules.title: Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with the City of Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken, such as a Notice to Quit or Summary Process. Tenants in multifamily apartment buildings must receive this information at lease signing or when eviction proceedings begin.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental agreements, including single residential dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to rental units in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, or in a non-profit facility that has the primary purpose of providing short term assistance, treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse. Does not apply to Short Term Rental Units as set forth in Article 4, Section 4.60 of the Cambridge Zoning Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: Most rental properties with five or more units are subject to rent control, which limits how much rent can be increased. 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most rental properties with five or more units are covered by rent control.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control. Other exemptions may apply if a property owner meets the criteria for one of the permitted exemptions.
rules.quoted_span:
(Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)
The Rent Control Ordinance provides certain exemptions from rent regulation.  A
"Rent Control Exemption Request"
can be submitted for the Office's review if a property owner meets the criteria for one of the permitted exemptions.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Other exemptions may apply if a property owner meets the criteria for one of the permitted exemptions.

rules.title: Motion to study and consider ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: If enacted, this would direct the City to consider banning the use of algorithm-based software to set rents in Los Angeles.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would apply citywide to rental housing if enacted.
rules.quoted_span: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set rents in the City.

rules.title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a tenancy without a listed just cause, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Tenants are protected after six months of occupancy or after the original lease expires, whichever comes first.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most residential rental properties in Los Angeles not regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Exempts transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to units covered by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Tenant must have lived in the unit for at least six months or the original lease must have expired, whichever comes first.

rules.title: Eviction Notices Filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: All eviction notices must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three business days of service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all JCO and RSO rental properties in Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent – Minimum Threshold
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant for non-payment of rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all RSO and JCO rental units in Los Angeles.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase under RSO
rules.requirement: For covered units, rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage set by the city. No additional percentage increase for utilities is allowed after February 2, 2026.
rules.key_value: allowable rent increase percentage (set by city)
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, including apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family units on the same parcel, and certain other unit types.
rules.exemptions: Condominiums and townhomes where tenancy commenced after December 31, 1995. Other exemptions may apply for luxury units or specific circumstances.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage (click here to view the allowable rent increase PDF). Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Protections under RSO
rules.requirement: Landlords may only evict tenants for legal reasons listed in the ordinance, including both at-fault and no-fault grounds. No-fault evictions require payment of tenant relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for listed legal reasons; relocation pay for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, including apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family units on the same parcel, and certain other unit types.
rules.exemptions: Condominiums and townhomes where tenancy commenced after December 31, 1995. Other exemptions may apply for luxury units or specific circumstances.
rules.quoted_span:
Legal Reasons for Eviction
Tenant is at-fault

Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit

rules.title: Eviction Notice Filing Requirement under RSO
rules.requirement: For any eviction of a tenant in a covered unit, the landlord must file the notice to terminate tenancy with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three business days of serving the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, including apartments, duplexes, two or more single-family units on the same parcel, and certain other unit types.
rules.exemptions: Condominiums and townhomes where tenancy commenced after December 31, 1995. Other exemptions may apply for luxury units or specific circumstances.
rules.quoted_span: All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO ) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within three (3) business days of service on the tenant per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase under RSO (2025-2026)
rules.requirement: For rental units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), the maximum allowable annual rent increase from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 is 3%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
rules.exemptions: Non-RSO properties are not covered.
rules.quoted_span: Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026 is 3%.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Coverage depends on whether the unit is subject to the RSO, which may require checking city records.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Evictions under RSO & JCO
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay relocation assistance to tenants for all no-fault evictions under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice. Tenants may use non-payment of relocation as a defense in eviction.
rules.key_value: $11,000–$27,400 per unit (2026-2027), depending on tenant status and length of tenancy; one month’s rent for certain single-family dwellings; higher amounts for low-income tenants displaced for new construction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to units covered by the RSO or JCO in Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include evicting a resident manager to replace with another, evictions due to hazardous conditions from natural disasters not caused by landlord negligence, and certain offsets for unpaid rent (except for government-ordered vacate or unpermitted dwellings).
rules.interaction: Relocation amounts increase annually and may be superseded by state law or the Resident Protections Ordinance for certain demolitions.
rules.quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO). Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Demolition for New Construction (Resident Protections Ordinance)
rules.requirement: Landlords demolishing Protected Units for new construction must pay relocation assistance to all tenants, with higher payments for low-income tenants (80% AMI or less), and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw with LAHD before eviction. Payment must be made within 15 days of notice, and tenants may receive standardized payments, a comparable replacement unit, or individualized relocation as determined by the City or a private consultant.
rules.key_value: $87,450–$115,480 for low-income tenants (2026-2027); $11,000–$27,400 for above low-income tenants; one month’s rent for certain single-family dwellings.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to demolition of Protected Units for new construction in Los Angeles, including all RSO units and units rented to low-income households within the past five years.
rules.exemptions: Relocation offset for unpaid rent except for government-ordered vacate or unpermitted dwellings. Exemptions for certain single-family dwellings owned by natural persons with four or fewer units.
rules.interaction: If state law (Housing Crisis Act) or the Resident Protections Ordinance requires higher payments, those apply. City rules apply unless preempted by state law.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.22-151.28, 165.03.I, 66300.6(b)(4)(A) (Gov. Code), Ordinances #188481 and #188482
rules.quoted_span: A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish for new construction is required to pay relocation assistance and to file a Declaration of Intent to Evict or Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental Housing Use with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) prior to evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: If enacted, this bill would prohibit algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market.
rules.coverage_conditions: Statewide, all rental housing.
