rules.requirement: If enacted, this bill would prohibit algorithmic rent setting in Massachusetts.
rules.coverage_conditions: If enacted, would apply statewide to rental housing.
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting

rules.title: General prohibition on rent control; limited municipal authority with strict conditions
rules.requirement: No city or town in Massachusetts may enact, maintain, or enforce rent control of any kind, except under a voluntary system with strict conditions, including compensation to owners and exemptions for small landlords and high-rent units.
rules.key_value: Rent control prohibited except under voluntary, compensated, and limited municipal programs
rules.coverage_conditions: All cities and towns in Massachusetts are prohibited from enacting rent control except as specified.
rules.exemptions: Exempts rental units owned by persons or entities owning less than ten rental units, and units with fair market rent exceeding $400. Also, any owner may decline to participate in local rent control after six months.
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides: (a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced, and the property of a person or entity declining to have his or its property subjected to such regulation shall be wholly unaffected by any aspect of the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation; (b) such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400; and (c) a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners of rent controlled units for each unit in the amount of the difference between the unit's fair market rent and the unit's below market, rent controlled rent, with such compensation coming from the municipality's general funds, so that the cost of any rent control shall be borne by all taxpayers of a municipality and not by the owners of regulated units only.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Any owner may opt out of local rent control after six months; exemption for units with fair market rent exceeding $400.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination in rental housing based on source of income (public assistance, housing subsidies)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or otherwise discriminate against applicants because they receive public assistance or housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing accommodations in Massachusetts.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination in rental housing based on familial status (presence of children)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or otherwise discriminate against applicants because they have children who will occupy the premises, except for certain small owner-occupied buildings and temporary subleases.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing accommodations in Massachusetts, except as stated in exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to (1) dwellings with three apartments or less, one of which is occupied by an elderly or infirm person for whom the presence of children would constitute a hardship; (2) temporary leasing or subleasing of a single family dwelling, apartment, or condo unit by the owner or sublessor who ordinarily occupies it as their principal residence, for up to one year; (3) leasing of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where the other unit is occupied by the owner as their residence.
rules.quoted_span: to refuse to rent or lease or sell or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person such accommodations because such person has a child or children who shall occupy the premises with such person or to discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of such accommodations or the acquisition thereof, or in the furnishing of facilities and services in connection therewith, because such person has a child or children who occupy or shall occupy the premises with such person; provided, however, that nothing herein shall limit the applicability of any local, state, or federal restrictions regarding the maximum number of persons permitted to occupy a dwelling. When the commission or a court finds that discrimination in violation of this paragraph has occurred with respect to a residential premises containing dangerous levels of lead in paint, plaster, soil, or other accessible material, notification of such finding shall be sent to the director of the childhood lead poisoning prevention program. This subsection shall not apply to: (1) Dwellings containing three apartments or less, one of which apartments is occupied by an elderly or infirm person for whom the presence of children would constitute a hardship. For purposes of this subsection, an ''elderly person'' shall mean a person sixty-five years of age or over, and an ''infirm person'' shall mean a person who is disabled or suffering from a chronic illness. (2) The temporary leasing or temporary subleasing of a single family dwelling, a single apartment, or a single unit of a condominium or housing cooperative, by the owner of such dwelling, apartment, or unit, or in the case of a subleasing, by the sublessor thereof, who ordinarily occupies the dwelling, apartment, or unit as his or her principal place of residence. For purposes of this subsection, the term ''temporary leasing'' shall mean leasing during a period of the owner's or sublessor's absence not to exceed one year. (3) The leasing of a single dwelling unit in a two family dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied by the owner as his residence.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Exemption for dwellings with three apartments or less, one of which is occupied by an elderly or infirm person for whom the presence of children would constitute a hardship, cannot be expressed with available fields.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination in rental housing based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, ancestry, age, marital status, veteran status, blindness, hearing impairment, or handicap
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent, lease, or sell, or otherwise discriminate in terms, conditions, or privileges of rental housing based on protected characteristics including race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, ancestry, age, marital status, veteran status, blindness, hearing impairment, or handicap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing accommodations in Massachusetts, except as stated in exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions for age restrictions in elderly housing, and for leasing of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the other unit is occupied by the owner as their residence.
rules.quoted_span: to refuse to rent or lease or sell or negotiate for sale or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person or group of persons such accommodations because of the race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, which shall not include persons whose sexual orientation involves minor children as the sex object, age, genetic information, ancestry, or marital status of such person or persons or because such person is a veteran or member of the armed forces, or because such person is blind, or hearing impaired or has any other handicap; (b) to discriminate against any person because of his race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, which shall not include persons whose sexual orientation involves minor children as the sex object, age, ancestry, or marital status or because such person is a veteran or member of the armed forces, or because such person is blind, or hearing impaired or has any other handicap in the terms, conditions or privileges of such accommodations or the acquisitions thereof, or in the furnishings of facilities and services in connection therewith, or because such a person possesses a trained dog guide as a consequence of blindness, or hearing impairment; (c) to cause to be made any written or oral inquiry or record concerning the race, religious creed, color, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, which shall not include persons whose sexual orientation involves minor children as the sex object, age, genetic information, ancestry or marital status of the person seeking to rent or lease or buy any such accommodation, or concerning the fact that such person is a veteran or a member of the armed forces or because such person is blind or hearing impaired or has any other handicap.

rules.title: Prohibition on discrimination in rental housing based on disability (reasonable accommodation and modification)
rules.requirement: Landlords must permit reasonable modifications and accommodations for tenants with disabilities, and may not refuse to rent because of a person's need for such modifications or accommodations. In multifamily buildings of 10 or more units, the owner must pay for reasonable modifications unless it would impose an undue hardship.
rules.key_value: Owner pays for modifications in buildings with 10+ units unless undue hardship; tenant pays otherwise.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental housing accommodations in Massachusetts, with specific requirements for publicly assisted housing, multiple dwelling housing of 10 or more units, or contiguously located housing of 10 or more units.
rules.exemptions: Owner is not required to pay for ramping a front entrance of more than five steps or for installing a wheelchair lift. Maximum of 10% of units required to be made fully accessible at owner's expense.
rules.quoted_span: For purposes of subsections 6 and 7 discrimination on the basis of handicap shall include but not be limited to: (1) a refusal to permit or to make, at the expense of the handicapped person, reasonable modification of existing premises occupied or to be occupied by such person if such modification is necessary to afford such person full enjoyment of such premises; provided, however, that, in the case of publicly assisted housing, multiple dwelling housing consisting of ten or more units, or contiguously located housing consisting of ten or more units, reasonable modification shall be at the expense of the owner or other person having the right of ownership; provided, further, that, in the case of public ownership of such housing units the cost of such reasonable modification shall be subject to appropriation; and provided, further, that, in the case of a rental, the landlord may, where the modification to be paid for by the handicapped person will materially alter the marketability of the housing, condition permission for a modification on the tenant agreeing to restore or pay for the cost of restoring, the interior of the premises to the condition that existed prior to such modification, reasonable wear and tear excepted; (2) a refusal to make reasonable accommodations in rules, policies, practices, or services, when such accommodations may be necessary to afford a handicapped person equal opportunity to use and enjoy a dwelling; and (3) discrimination against or a refusal to rent to a person because of such person's need for reasonable modification or accommodation.

rules.title: Determination of lease for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: A landlord must give at least 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent, but the tenant can stop the eviction by paying all rent due with interest and costs before the answer is due in court. If nonpayment was due to a government delay in rental payments, the court must continue the hearing for at least 7 days and allow the tenancy to continue if all rent, interest, and costs are paid within that time.
rules.key_value: 14 days' notice; cure by full payment before answer due
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all written residential leases in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: None stated for multifamily apartment buildings.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a tenancy at will by giving three months' written notice, or if rent is paid more frequently, by giving notice equal to the rent interval or thirty days, whichever is longer. For nonpayment of rent, a landlord may terminate with fourteen days' written notice, but the tenant can prevent termination by paying all rent due within ten days if they have not received a similar notice in the past twelve months.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice (or rent interval/30 days); 14 days for nonpayment with 10-day cure
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all estates at will (tenancies at will) in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: None stated for multifamily apartment buildings; special provisions for government payment delays and for tenants who have not received a similar notice in the past 12 months.
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer. ... In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

rules.title: Security deposit maximum and permitted move-in payments (until August 1, 2025)
rules.requirement: At or prior to the start of a tenancy, a landlord may not require more than first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the cost for a key and lock. No other move-in payments are allowed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in Massachusetts except as otherwise exempted.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.interaction: Superseded by amended language effective August 1, 2025.
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay any amount in excess of the following: (i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and, (ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and, (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent ... and, (iv) the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock.

rules.title: Security deposit maximum and permitted move-in payments (effective August 1, 2025)
rules.requirement: Starting August 1, 2025, a landlord or agent may not require more than first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the cost for a key and lock. Regulations may allow an optional fee in lieu of a security deposit, but the total of such fees and any security deposit may not exceed one month's rent.
rules.key_value: security deposit or fee in lieu = 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in Massachusetts except as otherwise exempted.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.interaction: Supersedes prior version of this section as of August 1, 2025.
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following: (i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and, (ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and, (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2);  provided, however, that the executive office of housing and livable communities may promulgate regulations to authorize a lessor and a tenant or prospective tenant to agree to the payment of a fee in lieu of payment of a security deposit; ... (C) limit the total sum of the fee or recurring payments, regardless of the duration of the lease and any extensions thereto, to an amount not to exceed 1 month's rent; ... provided further, that the sum of fees paid to waive a security deposit and the payment of the security deposit shall not exceed, in total, the amount of 1 month's rent; ... and, (iv) the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock.

rules.title: Security deposit handling: separate account, receipt, and interest
rules.requirement: A landlord must hold a security deposit in a separate, interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank, provide a receipt with bank details within 30 days, and pay the tenant 5% annual interest or the actual bank rate, whichever is less, each year or at move-out.
rules.key_value: 5% annual interest or actual bank rate
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in Massachusetts except as otherwise exempted.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth ... A receipt shall be given to the tenant within thirty days after such deposit is received by the lessor which receipt shall indicate the name and location of the bank in which the security deposit has been deposited and the amount and account number of said deposit.  Failure to comply with this paragraph shall entitle the tenant to immediate return of the security deposit. (b) A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

rules.title: Security deposit return deadline and allowable deductions
rules.requirement: A landlord must return the security deposit or balance within 30 days after the end of the tenancy, minus only unpaid rent, unpaid water charges, unpaid tax escalation, or reasonable repair costs for tenant-caused damage (excluding normal wear and tear). An itemized, sworn list of damages and receipts must be provided for any deductions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in Massachusetts except as otherwise exempted.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;  provided, however, that the lessor may deduct from such security deposit for the following: (i) any unpaid rent or water charges ... (ii) any unpaid increase in real estate taxes ... (iii) a reasonable amount necessary to repair any damage caused to the dwelling unit by the tenant ... In the case of such damage, the lessor shall provide to the tenant within such thirty days an itemized list of damages, sworn to by the lessor or his agent under pains and penalties of perjury, itemizing in precise detail the nature of the damage and of the repairs necessary to correct such damage, and written evidence, such as estimates, bills, invoices or receipts, indicating the actual or estimated cost thereof.

rules.title: Security deposit forfeiture and treble damages for violations
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to comply with deposit account, itemized list, or return requirements, the tenant is entitled to three times the amount of the deposit or balance, plus 5% interest, court costs, and attorney's fees.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties in Massachusetts except as otherwise exempted.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: If the lessor or his agent fails to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

rules.title: Reprisal for reporting violations of law or for tenant's union activity; damages and costs; notice of termination, presumption; waiver in leases or other rental agreements prohibited
rules.requirement: If a landlord gives a notice of termination (except for nonpayment of rent), rent increase, or substantial change in terms within six months after a tenant reports violations, joins a tenants' union, or takes similar protected actions, it is presumed to be retaliation unless the landlord proves otherwise by clear and convincing evidence. Any waiver of this protection in a lease is void.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental premises in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to termination for nonpayment of rent. Exemptions for hotels, motels, hospitals, and similar are not stated here.
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities. Such presumption shall be rebutted only by clear and convincing evidence that such person's action was not a reprisal against the tenant and that such person had sufficient independent justification for taking such action, and would have in fact taken such action, in the same manner and at the same time the action was taken, regardless of tenants engaging in, or the belief that tenants had engaged in, activities protected under this section.

rules.title: Real estate brokers and salesmen; persons finding dwelling accommodations for fee; contracts; payment of fee
rules.requirement: After August 1, 2025, only the party (landlord or tenant) who originally engaged and contracted with a licensed broker or salesperson may be required to pay a broker's fee for finding a rental unit. Tenants cannot be charged a broker fee unless they hired the broker themselves.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental residential real property transactions involving a broker or salesperson in Massachusetts.
rules.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 112, § 87DDD 1/2 (as amended by 2025, 9, Sec. 43)
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must include specific form and information
rules.requirement: A landlord must provide a specific form with information about rental assistance, legal rights, and a prominent statement when giving a notice to quit for nonpayment of rent. Courts will not accept an eviction filing for nonpayment without proof that this form was delivered to the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – Ban on Pre-Conditional Offer Criminal Record Inquiry
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer, except for methamphetamine manufacture in federally assisted housing or lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. Exemptions for federally assisted housing regarding methamphetamine manufacture and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer, except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – Limits on Types of Criminal Records Considered
rules.requirement: Landlords may not consider arrests not resulting in conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated, nullified, juvenile, or sealed records at any stage of the rental process.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records: (1) arrests or charges that have not resulted in a criminal conviction; (2) expunged convictions; (3) convictions erased through executive pardon; (4) vacated and otherwise legally nullified convictions; (5) juvenile adjudications of delinquency; and (6) records that have been sealed.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – Post-Conditional Offer Criminal Record Consideration Limits
rules.requirement: After a conditional offer, landlords may only consider certain recent convictions and must conduct an individualized assessment before withdrawing an offer.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span: After the issuance of a conditional offer to an applicant, a housing provider may only consider a criminal record in the applicant’s history that: (1) resulted in a conviction for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault in violation of N.J.S.2C:14-2, causing or permitting a child to engage in a prohibited sexual act or in the simulation of such an act in violation of paragraph (3) of subsection b. of N.J.S.2C:24-4, or any crime that resulted in lifetime registration in a state sex offender registry; (2) is for an indictable offense of the first degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within the six years immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer; (3) is for an indictable offense of the second or third degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within the four years immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer; or (4) is for an indictable offense of the fourth degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within one year immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – Ban on Drug or Alcohol Testing and Drug Treatment Information Requests
rules.requirement: Landlords may not require applicants to submit to drug or alcohol tests or request consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

rules.title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge more than $50 as an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property, except for one- or two-family dwellings or real estate licensees who are not the landlord. The $50 cap will be adjusted annually for inflation starting January 1 of the year after enactment.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers all residential rental properties except one- or two-family dwellings and non-landlord real estate licensees.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a dwelling unit located in a one-family or two-family dwelling that is offered for rent; or a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission, unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.

rules.title: Security Deposit Maximum and Handling
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect more than one and one-half times one month's rent as a security deposit, and any additional yearly increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. The deposit must be held in trust, not commingled, and must be returned within 30 days after tenancy ends, with interest and an itemized list of deductions if any.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; 10% annual increase cap; 30-day return deadline
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing. Seasonal rentals (not more than 125 consecutive days) are also exempt.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit. ... Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1). Deductions may include the cost of any damages over and above normal wear and tear, and any other money due the landlord under the terms of the lease. The landlord must return the money either by personal delivery, registered, or certified mail. If there are any deductions made from the security deposit by the landlord, an itemized list of these deductions must also be sent to the tenant by registered or certified mail within 30 days from the termination of the tenancy.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest and Notice Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits to tenants annually or credit it toward rent, and must notify tenants in writing of the bank/investment company, amount, account type, and interest rate within 30 days of deposit and annually.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing. Seasonal rentals (not more than 125 consecutive days) are also exempt.
rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the renewal or anniversary of the tenant’s lease or on January 31, if the tenant has been given written notice, that the interest payments will be paid on January 31 of each year (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 (c)). Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at the time of each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking institution or investment company in which the money is deposited, the amount of the deposit, type of account, and current rate of interest for the account.

rules.title: Security Deposit Use for Rent if Landlord Fails to Pay Interest or Give Notice
rules.requirement: If the landlord fails to pay interest or provide required notice, the tenant may apply the security deposit plus 7% interest to rent after giving written notice and 30 days for the landlord to comply.
rules.key_value: 7% per annum if not paid/notice not given
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing. Seasonal rentals (not more than 125 consecutive days) are also exempt.
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant does not receive proper notice or is not paid interest as required, the tenant may use the security deposit for payment of rent by giving the landlord written notice that the security money plus interest at the rate of 7% per annum be applied to rent payments or payments due or to become due from the tenant. However, if the tenant does not receive the annual notice at the time of the annual interest payment, or is not paid the annual interest, as required, the tenant must give the landlord written notice and allow the landlord 30 days to comply with the annual interest payment and notice requirements. If the landlord does not reply within the allotted time, the tenant can use his security deposit toward his rent. If the tenant’s security deposit gets applied to his rent, the landlord may not make further demand for an additional security deposit (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19.1 (c)).

rules.title: Security Deposit Return After Displacement by Fire, Flood, Condemnation, or Evacuation
rules.requirement: If a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit within five business days and notify the tenant within three business days where it can be collected.
rules.key_value: 5 business days for return; 3 business days for notice
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing. Seasonal rentals (not more than 125 consecutive days) are also exempt.
rules.quoted_span: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit. ... Within three (3) business days of having received notice of the displacement, the landlord must let the tenant know where the security deposit can be collected.

rules.title: Penalty for Failure to Return Security Deposit
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within 30 days, or wrongfully withholds it, the tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees.
rules.key_value: Double damages plus costs and fees
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing. Seasonal rentals (not more than 125 consecutive days) are also exempt.
rules.quoted_span: If a landlord fails to return the security deposit within 30 days, or the tenant disagrees with the amount deducted, the tenant may sue for double the amount of the security deposit that the tenant contends was wrongfully withheld. If the tenant is successful, the court may award the tenant double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Security Deposit Handling on Sale or Transfer of Property
rules.requirement: If the property is sold or transferred, the new owner is responsible for the investment, notices, interest, and return of the security deposit, regardless of whether the deposit was transferred.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing. Seasonal rentals (not more than 125 consecutive days) are also exempt.
rules.quoted_span: If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner. Whether or not the deposit and interest are transferred, the new owner is responsible for the investment of the security deposit, giving all notices and paying interest, and for the return of the security deposit, plus any accrued earnings or interest (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21).

rules.title: Exemption of newly constructed multiple dwellings from local rent control
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for 30 years after completion of construction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt from local rent control ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.unstructured_conditions: The exemption period is calculated from the completion of construction, which may not be directly available as occupancy_date.

rules.title: No statewide rent control; unconscionable rent increases prohibited
rules.requirement: There is no statewide rent control, but rent increases must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental units in New Jersey.
rules.citation: Fromet Properties v. Buel, 294 N.J. Super. 601 (App. Div. 1996); Hale v. Farrakhan, 390 N.J. Super. 335 (App. Div. 2007)
rules.quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: Rent increases after conversion to condominium/cooperative/fee simple
rules.requirement: Rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from conversion to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.exemptions: Does not prohibit increases for new services or amenities.
rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: Just Cause Required for Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a dwelling unit used as a residence only by consent of the tenants or through the legal process of eviction. No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including apartment buildings and complexes.
rules.exemptions: This law may not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units. It does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant. Additionally, this law does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family, if that family member is developmentally disabled, and permanently occupies the dwelling unit.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for Eviction Due to Illegal Occupancy
rules.requirement: Any tenant evicted due to illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent. The landlord is responsible for paying the tenant’s relocation expenses.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants evicted due to illegal occupancy.
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent. The landlord is responsible f or paying the tenant’s relocation expenses.

rules.title: Notice Requirements for Eviction
rules.requirement: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction for most causes, with longer periods for certain grounds such as conversion or retirement from residential use.
rules.key_value: Varies by cause (1 month to 3 years)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including apartment buildings and complexes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units, hotels, motels, guest houses for transient or seasonal tenants, and certain family trust units.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d)).

rules.title: Prohibition of Self-Help Evictions
rules.requirement: A landlord or any other person who enters an apartment or property without a court order authorizing such entry and/or holds a tenant’s belongings unlawfully by force or threat of monies owed may be liable for damages to the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential rental properties.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or any other person who enters an apartment or property without a court order authorizing such entry and/or holds a tenant’s belongings unlawfully by force or threat of monies owed may be liable for damages to the tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-1).

rules.title: Prohibition on Source of Income Discrimination in Housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent to tenants based solely on their source of lawful income, including Section 8 HUD vouchers.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, except as listed in the exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Exempts: (1) rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit as their residence; (2) rental of a room or rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner as their residence; (3) preference by a religious organization for persons of the same religion; (4) familial status discrimination prohibition does not apply to housing for older persons.
rules.quoted_span: The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for rental property owners or their agents to use or pay for algorithmic revenue management software or any algorithmic device that performs a coordinating function to set or recommend rents, or for any person to perform a coordinating function that facilitates parallel pricing coordination among rental property owners.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers all rental residential dwelling units in New Jersey, including apartments and multifamily buildings.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to government entities setting or limiting rents through affordability controls, or to inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, or detention/correctional facilities.
rules.interaction: Municipalities are prohibited from enacting ordinances that conflict with this act.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a. a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator; ... e. any person to perform a coordinating function.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which includes only the specific at-fault and no-fault grounds listed in the ordinance. If you receive a notice to vacate, check if it states a listed just cause reason.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; see listed grounds
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties in San Diego, except those listed in §98.0703.
rules.exemptions: Hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted affordable housing (except Section 8), mobilehomes under state law, nonprofit hospitals/care/dorms, shared facilities with owner, certain owner-occupied buildings, new construction (CO within 15 years), and single-family homes/condos with qualifying ownership and notice.
rules.interaction: The ordinance supplements state law and does not override stricter tenant protections.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Exemption for single-family homes/condos requires both qualifying ownership (not REIT/corporation/LLC with corporate member) and written notice to tenant; cannot be determined from building data alone.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Eviction
rules.requirement: If you are evicted for a no-fault reason, your landlord must provide relocation assistance equal to two months' rent, or three months' rent if you are a senior or disabled, either as a direct payment or rent waiver.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants evicted for no-fault just cause under this Division.
rules.exemptions: Same as general coverage exemptions in §98.0703.
rules.interaction: Relocation assistance is credited against any other required by law and is in addition to return of security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice. (ii) If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Exemption for single-family homes/condos requires both qualifying ownership (not REIT/corporation/LLC with corporate member) and written notice to tenant; cannot be determined from building data alone.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. Landlords may not use software that calculates rent or occupancy recommendations based on nonpublic competitor data.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers all residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to software that only publishes reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from public information, and does not recommend future rental rates or occupancy levels; does not apply to software used to establish rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord for use in setting rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers all residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to software that only publishes reports from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or from public information, and does not recommend future rental rates or occupancy levels; does not apply to software used to establish rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement under San Francisco Rent Ordinance
rules.requirement: A landlord may only evict a tenant from a covered rental unit for one of the 17 listed 'just cause' reasons, and the dominant motive for eviction must be a just cause. Expiration of a lease or change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Some tenancies exempt from rent increase limitations (including newly constructed units first occupied after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins eligible units, and some government-regulated units) are still subject to just cause eviction rules. Exemptions for hotels, hospitals, dormitories, etc. are not listed here.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase for Rent-Controlled Units (2026-2027)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the maximum annual rent increase allowed from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rent-controlled units in San Francisco.
rules.exemptions: Units not subject to rent control are exempt.
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Ordinance (annual allowable increase announcement)
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.unstructured_conditions: Covers only units subject to San Francisco rent control; coverage depends on local rent control status.

rules.title: Prohibition on Algorithmic Devices for Rent Setting
rules.requirement: Landlords and others may not sell or use algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.key_value: Prohibits sale or use of algorithmic devices for rent setting
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential units in San Francisco.
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.requirement: If you are evicted for owner/relative move-in, demolition, permanent removal, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation, you are entitled to a relocation payment of $8,245.00 per tenant, up to $24,733.00 per unit, plus $5,497.00 for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children, for notices served between 3/01/26 and 2/28/27.

rules.title: Allowable Rent Increase for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.requirement: For covered rental units, the maximum allowable rent increase from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most multifamily rental units subject to the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Certain newer construction, single-family homes, and other exempt units as defined by the Rent Ordinance.

rules.title: Security Deposit Interest Rate for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay 4.2% annual interest on security deposits held from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 for covered units.

rules.title: Maximum Allowable Rent Increase
rules.requirement: Landlords may not increase rent by more than 3% or 80% of the CPI change, whichever is less, per year. For the period September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027, the maximum allowable rent increase is 2.87%.
rules.key_value: 3% or 80% of CPI, whichever is less (2.87% for 2026-2027)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to covered rental units in Santa Ana.
rules.exemptions: Not specified in the provided text.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a valid reason, such as nonpayment of rent, lease violation, or owner move-in, to evict a tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to covered rental units in Santa Ana.
rules.exemptions: Not specified in the provided text.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for covered residential units are capped at the lower of 3% or 80% of the CPI change over the most recent 12 months. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is allowed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental units in buildings constructed on or before February 1, 1995.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, or to mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance (as described in City announcement)
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days, a landlord may not terminate a tenancy except for specified just cause reasons, which must be stated in writing. For no-fault evictions, the landlord must provide either 3 months' relocation assistance or waive the last 3 months' rent.
rules.key_value: just cause required after 30 days; 3 months' relocation or rent waiver for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental units except those produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotels, hospitals, dormitories, and certain shared living quarters.
rules.exemptions: Exempts housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (as described in City announcement)
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
